newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Dec 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Dec 4.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The leaders of the ruling coalition agree that the government proposal for the 1997 state budget should not change in any way after its approval during December's meeting.
- Eurotel has announced price decreases of 20-50 percent for six types of mobile phones while their activation costs will also decrease by one third.'

- Velkomoravska Banka, which was placed under forced administration in July, will begin paying out clients' deposits starting Monday, according to the current administrator, Tomas Uvira. The reason the bank's deposits were unfrozen is the bank's current good liquidity.

- The expected increase of prices for rent and utilities as a result of the gradual deregulation, will go against efforts to keep the inflation rate down. Massive price deregulation is expected next July.

- While the State Environment Fund should receive five billion crowns next year, only 100 million crowns will be available for the support of environmental projects. The amount of funds available for this purpose should increase to two billion crowns in 1998.

- The Czech Army has too much heavy artillery for its size, in spite of the fact that the amount has decreased by practically 50 percent since 1993, according to the chairman of the parliamentary council for defense and security.
- Siemens is building a new factory to manufacture electronic compnents in Kaplice. The factory, with 3,000 square metres, will cost 34.5 million crowns to build.
MLADA FRONTA DNES - While many financial experts believe the Czech state budget could finsih the year with a deficit, a slight budget deficit is no cause for alarm.

PRAVO - The average price of medicine from Leciva Praha will increase by five or six percent in 1997, according to the company's general manager, Jiri Michal. The price increases will affect approximately one fifth of the comapny's 290 medicines and some medicines will actually decrease in price.
- Trade and Industry Minister, Vladimir Dlouhy, is travelling to China today where he will meet with senior politicians and industrial leaders.
